prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1433; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim file purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this call?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was driving home on a two-lane road in Houston, going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane while trying to pass a slow truck. I braked and turned, but we still met nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me forward and back.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?

A: No, nothing deployed. My seatbelt locked up and held me, though.

Q: Were you able to drive your car from the scene?

A: No. The front end was pushed in and the hood wouldn't close right, so a tow truck took it.

Q: Did you feel any pain or symptoms right away?

A: Not immediately. By that evening my neck was stiff, and by the next morning I had a dull ache across my shoulders and a headache at the base of my skull. Turning my head to check mirrors hurts now.

Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the following day and was referred to a physical therapist. I'm still going to sessions twice a week.

Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this accident?

A: Nothing serious. I had some occasional stiffness from sitting at a desk, but I wasn't in treatment for anything.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I've missed a few days of work because of the pain, and I'd like to be reimbursed for those and for my therapy costs.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up in writing with next steps.

A: Okay, thank you.
